newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's ENEL says seeking telecoms allies.
newsitem.headline: Italy's ENEL says seeking telecoms allies.

text.p: Italy's state electricity group Enel is actively looking for partners with an aim to break into the fixed-line and mobile telecommunications sector, chairman Chicco Testa was quoted as saying.

He said in an interview with Turin daily La Stampa that Enel, slated for privatisation this year, had technology, structures and networks which all could be enhanced with its entry into the telecommunications market in view of the sector's liberalisation due from 1998.
"We intend to dedicate ourselves to mobile and fixed-line telephony and this is not just a short-term commitment like bidding for Italy's third mobile phone operating licence.
"Telecoms does not represent Enel's core business and therefore we need a partner operating in this field," he said.
Testa said it was already known that Enel was in talks with France Telecom "as well as other European, American and Canadian groups."
"AT&T has problems in Europe but contacts with them are going on," he said, adding that Enel weas also in touch with Cable & Wireless and Unisource.
He said it was possible Enel would have more than one ally, "in fact we also need a financial partner."
Any telecoms company eventually set up could be listed on the stock market, he said.
"I think we will have clearer ideas in two to three months," he added.
